product_name: Nova NHT 1076 Cordless Beard Trimmer for Men (Black & Blue)
reviews: [★5] Cheap emergency trimmer - Good enough for trimming sideburns and quick touch-ups before college presentations.
[★5] Very low price tag - For under 400 rupees you get a functional cordless trimmer with charging cable and oil.
[★5] Lightweight plastic body - Extremely light in hand and easy to pack into a gym wash bag.
[★5] Decent for thin stubble - If your beard is soft and sparse, it cuts reasonably well without stalling.
[★4] Compact travel companion - Small form factor fits into any toiletry kit for weekend trips.
[★4] Includes basic guide comb - Plastic comb attachment lets you select 4 different length settings.
[★4] Works fine when fully charged - First 10 minutes of run time deliver sufficient blade speed.
[★4] Simple to clean - Removable blade head allows brushing out trapped hair fragments under the cutter.
[★4] Fair budget purchase - Expected cheap performance for 389 rupees, and it meets modest expectations.
[★3] Extremely long 8-hour charge time - Requires overnight 8-10 hour charging for barely 25 minutes of cordless trimming.
[★3] Comb adjustment slips easily - Pressing slightly too hard against jawline causes the comb guide to slide and trim too short.
[★3] Loud and buzzy motor - High-pitched whining sound and heavy vibration make hand numb after 5 minutes.
[★3] No battery percentage indicator - Simple red LED stays lit continuously and never changes color or turns off when full.
[★3] Non-waterproof construction - Cannot wash blade under running tap without risking motor rusting or short circuit.
[★2] Painfully pulls and tugs facial hair - Stainless steel blades are dull and snag coarse beard hair instead of cutting cleanly.
[★2] Battery drains in 12 minutes - Motor noticeably slows down after just one side of face, chewing through hair painfully.
[★2] Gets dangerously hot near blade - Blade teeth heat up to uncomfortable temperatures after 7 minutes of continuous operation.
[★2] Extremely fragile plastic comb - One of the comb teeth snapped off when attempting to detach it for cleaning.
[★2] Uneven trimming results - Leaves patchy uneven lengths across cheek line requiring multiple frustrating passes.
[★2] Slow cutting speed - Takes twice as long to groom beard compared to a standard Philips trimmer.
[★2] Flimsy proprietary charging cable - 2-pin barrel plug is loose and disconnects if moved on the counter.
[★2] Zero customer support - Nova warranty contact numbers either ring indefinitely or disconnect automatically.
[★1] Complete waste of money - Stopped turning on after the third charge cycle. Internal battery has zero lifespan.
[★1] Severe razor burns and cuts - Chewed into skin near the jawline causing bloody nicks and skin irritation.
[★1] Motor stalled on medium beard - Motor jammed completely on a 5mm beard and began emitting an acrid burning plastic smell.
[★1] Battery dead on arrival - Kept on charge for 12 hours and motor died after exactly 30 seconds of spinning.
[★1] Poor build quality - Feels like cheap hollow recycled plastic that would shatter if dropped on tiles.
[★1] Blades rusted within 3 weeks - Moisture in bathroom cabinet caused brown rust spots on the cutting blade.
[★1] Misleading cordless claims - Must stay plugged into wall adapter to have enough power to cut coarse hair.
[★1] Absolute junk - Do not waste 400 rupees on this hazard. Invest in a proper branded trimmer.
